plans.note: Review Section 21 for cap amount, mutuality and consequential-loss exclusion; check the 'Excluded Claims' definition in Section 1 for the carve-out list (IP indemnity, confidentiality, data breach, wilful misconduct) and confirm it is not capped or one-sided in Vendor's favour.

Section 20 is the indemnity home: confirm Vendor IP infringement and misconduct/data-breach indemnities run to us, that any Customer indemnity is narrow, and that indemnity interacts correctly with Excluded Claims (Section 1) and the cap (Section 21).

No dedicated restrictive-covenant section in the outline; if a non-compete exists it would be buried in Customer Responsibilities (12), Compliance (26) or General (30). Flag only if language restricts our business lines or competing products.
Check the scope language in Section 2 and Order Form mechanics in Section 4 for sole-source/exclusive-supplier wording, and Section 12 for any obligation to route all similar work to Vendor.
Pricing MFN language would sit in Section 7 (Fees) or as a General clause; accept MFN in our favour but resist any obligation on us to extend Vendor our best terms or disclose competitor pricing.
Non-solicit typically appears in General (30) or Customer Responsibilities (12); if binding us, seek 12-month limit, named-personnel scope and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out.

Section 9 governs termination rights: confirm we have convenience termination on reasonable notice without termination fees, and that Vendor has no reciprocal mid-term convenience right; check Section 10 for any early-termination charges.
Section 8 should be reviewed for auto-renewal length, the non-renewal notice window (target 30 days, resist 90+) and any uncapped uplift, cross-checking escalation language in Section 7.
Section 28 sets law and forum; verify it selects NY, DE, CA or England & Wales with court jurisdiction rather than offshore or foreign-seat arbitration (note Vendor is a UK entity).

Section 24 covers assignment and change of control: secure our right to assign to Affiliates and successors without consent, and delete any Vendor termination right triggered by our change of control.

Section 14 should vest Deliverables in us and Section 15 confirm we own Customer Data; check the Deliverable, Customer Data and Vendor Technology definitions in Section 1 and any feedback/licence-back grants in Section 13.

Section 13 is the licence grant: confirm scope extends to our Affiliates and contractors/users, and that the grant is not revocable or suspendable at Vendor's discretion; check Affiliate order mechanics in Section 4.

Section 22 sets Vendor audits of our usage — press for once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, remote/off-site where possible, Vendor's cost absent material underpayment; Section 23 records obligations may extend the same right.

Look for interest/late-fee or liquidated damages payable by us in Section 7 and any penalty language in Section 21; service credits owed to us under Section 3 service levels are acceptable and should not be an exclusive remedy.

Section 19 warranties: confirm a professional-services and conformity warranty of at least 90 days with re-performance plus refund remedy, and check that Section 6 acceptance and Section 3 performance terms do not cut the warranty short or disclaim it.

Section 18 exists — verify coverage types and limits (commercial general, professional/E&O, cyber) given Vendor hosts our data under Sections 15 and 17, plus certificate and notice-of-cancellation obligations.
Check Sections 7 and 4 for committed spend, minimum volumes, non-reducible seat counts or take-or-pay true-ups; if present, pair with a downward flex right or convenience exit under Section 9.

Section 11 should provide transition assistance and data return — confirm a defined assistance period at agreed rates, return in a usable format, and deletion certification consistent with Sections 10 and 15.
